transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, uh… I’m here because work’s gotten hard in a way I can’t really explain. I’m a construction manager, so I’m supposed to be the guy walking sites, checking things, making sure crews are set up right—and I’ve done that for years.

But now, every time I have to get near a scaffold, or a roof edge, or one of those upper platforms, my head just tells me I’m about to go over. Even when I can see the rails are there, even when I know the setup is supposed to be safe. It’s like my brain doesn’t care what I know.

And it’s frustrating because I’ll be standing there thinking about the job, the schedule, whether the concrete guys are holding us up again—sorry, that’s not really the point—but then I get near the edge and it’s like everything narrows to that one thought: I’m going over.
Does this fear come on only when you’re up high or near an edge?

Yeah—well, I mean, mostly when I’m up high or right near something where there’s a drop. Like if I’m coming up on a scaffold, or a roof edge, or one of those upper platforms, that’s when it hits. 

It’s strange because I can look right at the guardrails and know, logically, everything’s set up the way it’s supposed to be—same stuff I’ve checked a hundred times for crews—but my head still goes, “You’re about to go over.” Then I start thinking about that instead of the actual job.
Have you ever had one of these episodes when you were not up high or near an edge?

No, not really. It’s tied to being up high or right near a drop—scaffolds, roof edges, upper platforms, that kind of thing. I mean, I can be walking around the rest of the site thinking about deliveries or whether somebody put the wrong materials in the wrong place, and I’m fine. But once I get near an edge, even if the rails are there and I know it’s supposed to be safe, my head just goes straight to, “You’re going over.”
